arguments.text: Settle now. Long smooth strokes, find your race rhythm.

10 km, 8 legs of 1250 m out-and-back. Calibration: pod CP 158 W shaft, boat CP 100 W (may be 10-25 pct off). Plan: settle after hard start to about pod CP (155-165 W shaft), keep pod reserve (w_bal_pod_frac) above 0.3 until 2 km to go, then spend it; final sprint (finish) at about 600 m to go. Compare legs in same direction to judge current and fade. Watch for incidents (rudder weed, pod drift, radio course changes).

arguments.message: Pod reserve below 25 pct: check effort, consider ease
Boat slower than pod power predicts vs fitted current: possible weed on rudder or drag change (check turns)
Pod shaft power over 112 pct of CP for a minute after the start

text: Cued ease to about 160 ground pace after hard start (pod reserve 56 pct, emptying in 270 m); set plan and three watches (reserve low, drag jump, overcook).

arguments.text: Ease off now, too hot. Lighter strokes, settle into race pace.

Min 2.2: first ease cue (min 1.1, pace 160) not followed much: pod stayed 220-230 W. Pod reserve 0.19 at 450 m. Second ease cue sent (pace 162). If still over 180 W pod by min 4, consider that CP may be higher than calibrated (paddler resisting) or cue again.

arguments.reason: check whether second ease cue was followed

text: Cued ease again (pace 162): pod reserve at 0.19 and still draining after the hard start.

arguments.text: Back off more. Easy for two minutes, breathe, recover.

Min 3.5: both reserve models read 0; pod 185 W (CP 158). Paddler says 10/10, close to my limit: consistent with calibration, no evidence CP is higher. Cued ease to 166 ground pace (current +0.2 helps on leg 1) to let reserve refill. Target after recovery: pod about 155 W.

arguments.reason: check recovery and reset effort to about CP

text: Cued ease to 166: reserve empty and paddler at 10/10, so recover before settling at critical power.

arguments.text: Good. Hold this effort through the turn, ignore the pace.

Min 5.7: recovered to pod 154 W (CP 158), pod reserve 0.03, boat reserve 0.10. Leg 1 (north) has push +0.2 to +0.25 m/s helping, so return legs (south) go into it: do NOT give ground pace targets that suit leg 1 on south legs (about 20-25 s/500 slower ground pace there at the same effort). Cued hold by effort, no pace, before turn 1.

10 km, 8 legs of 1250 m out-and-back (north legs 1,3,5,7 have about +0.2 m/s current helping; south legs 2,4,6,8 against). Start went too hard: reserve emptied by min 3.5, paddler 10/10. Plan now: hold pod shaft power about 152-160 W (CP 158) by effort, no ground-pace targets across directions; let reserve rebuild a little; from about 2 km to go spend what reserve there is; finish cue at about 500-600 m to go. Watch for incidents (rudder weed, pod drift, radio course changes).

arguments.message: Pod shaft power under 88 pct of CP for a minute: blow-up, over-easing, or incident

text: Cued hold by effort (no pace) before turn into the current; pod now at CP after recovery; updated plan and added under-power watch.

arguments.reason: paddler said legs going, close to limit at turn 1 (min 6.3); pod 154 W at CP, reserve 4 pct: reassure cue once gate opens, unless power has collapsed

text: no cue: gate closed for 25 s; set wake-up to reassure paddler (at CP, reserve rebuilding slowly).

arguments.text: Slow display is the current. Your effort is perfect, keep it.

text: Reassure cue: paddler at CP on the into-current leg, display pace slow from the current, not from effort.

arguments.text: Just a touch lighter. Smooth and long, save it for later.

arguments.message: Pod power creeping above CP with pod reserve under 10 pct

arguments.text: Min 9.8 (leg 2, into current -0.16): pod crept up 155 -> 165 W with pod reserve 0, boat reserve 1 pct; fade at same rate about 0 pct. Cued a small ease (no pace). If paddler holds 160-165 W for 10+ min with empty reserve and no fade, CP may be higher than 158: consider set_critical_power (cp_shaft_w about 165).

text: Cued a small ease: pod 165 W, 4 pct over CP with an empty reserve; added watch for creeping above CP.

arguments.text: You are over the limit. Ease back to 178 pace, steady.

arguments.reason: just after turn 2 onto the north leg (current helps): replace the 178 pace target, which is too slow there, with hold by effort or about 158 pace

arguments.text: Min 11.4: pod crept to 171 W, boat 108 W (both over CP, both reserves 0); ease cue without pace at 9.9 ignored; paddler 10/10 close to limit. Work above CP so far is about 10-20 pct more than W 12.7 kJ, no forced drop yet: W or CP maybe slightly underestimated, but paddler is at the edge. Cued ease pace 178 for the rest of leg 2 (into current = about CP). MUST re-cue after turn 2 (north leg needs about 158 ground pace for CP).

text: Cued ease to 178 pace (about CP into the current): pod 171 W over CP with empty reserve, paddler 10/10; wake set after the turn to retarget.

arguments.text: Strong and steady. Hold this rhythm through the turn.

arguments.reason: Since min 8.5 paddler has held pod 158-171 W and boat 104-108 W with both reserves reading empty, no forced drop and no fade at the same rate; two ease cues ignored. Work above calibrated CP is about 25 pct more than the calibrated reserve, so CP looks about 4 pct low (inside the stated 10-25 pct error).

arguments.text: 10 km, 8 legs of 1250 m out-and-back (north legs 1,3,5,7: current about +0.2 helps; south legs 2,4,6,8 against). Hard start emptied reserve by min 3.5. CP corrected at min 13.3 to pod 164 W / boat 104 W (paddler held above old CP with empty reserve, no fade); reserves after correction pod 12 pct, boat 17 pct. Paddler ignores ease cues and paces by own feel at about pod 165-170 / boat 106 / 3.0 m/s water; says near limit (10/10) every time. Plan: let them hold their own steady effort, use reassure/hold, no ground-pace targets across directions. Watch for blow-up (under_power) and incidents (weed on rudder, pod drift, radio course change). From about 1.5-2 km to go spend reserve; finish cue at about 500 m to go.

Min 13.3: ease cue with pace 178 also ignored (pod 170 -> 168). Paddler: Really feeling it now, near my limit. Set CP to pod 164 / boat 104 (1 of 3 uses). Cued hold through turn 2 (replaces 178 pace target). Within leg 2 pod rose 158 -> 171 while boat model rose only 104 -> 107 as fitted current shrank -0.21 -> -0.14: genuine effort rise most likely, but keep an eye on pod/boat ratio (eta_est about 0.62) for pod drift.

text: Cued hold through turn 2 (overrides old pace target); corrected CP up about 4 pct on evidence of no forced drop; updated plan.

arguments.text: Normal dip. Breathe, light hands, long strokes. It comes back.

arguments.reason: Blow-up at min 15.5-16 (pod 176 -> 122 W, fade -8.5 pct) right after 2 min at 176 W: true reserve is empty now, while CP 164 read 13 pct; old CP 158 read empty from min 3.5 although paddler held 165-171 for 5 min. Truth is between: 162 W pod, 102.5 W boat.
check recovery after blow-up at min 16; then set a steady target below CP to rebuild (north leg about 162-166 ground pace, south leg about 178-182)

arguments.text: Min 16.3: BLOW-UP. After hold cue at turn 2 pod went to 176 W for 2 min, then dropped to 122 W (boat 79 W, fade -8.5 pct, pod/boat ratio normal so not weed). True reserve empty now. CP reset to pod 162 / boat 102.5 (2 of 3 uses; reads 9 pct pod now, so treat reserve readings as about 9 pct too high). Lesson: this paddler surges above 170 W on own feel and blows; give explicit pace targets per leg to cap at about 160 pod (north legs ground about 160-162, south legs about 178-180).

text: Reassure cue during blow-up (pod 122 W, forced below CP); CP reset to 162 W pod; wake in 100 s to set a capped target.

arguments.text: 10 km, 8 legs of 1250 m out-and-back (north legs 1,3,5,7: current about +0.15 helps; south legs 2,4,6,8: about -0.15 against). Blew up at min 16 after surging to 176 W pod on own feel; forced to about 124 W. CP now pod 162 / boat 102.5 (2 of 3 corrections used); pod reserve reading is probably about 9 pct too high. Plan: let them recover, then CAP effort near pod 155-160 with an explicit ground-pace target re-set at every turn (north legs about 162, south legs about 180); do not cue hold without a pace (paddler drifts up and blows). Spend what reserve remains from about 1.5 km to go; finish cue at about 500 m to go. Watch for incidents (weed on rudder, pod drift, radio course change).

text: no cue: under-power alert is the known blow-up; gate closed 28 s; plan updated, pending wake at min 18 will set a capped target.

arguments.text: Recovered. Now cap it: ease to 162 pace, steady and smooth.

arguments.reason: just after turn 3 onto south leg 4 (into current): replace 162 target with about 180 ground pace (hold)

arguments.text: Min 18.1: blow-up lasted about 2 min at 124-134 W; back to 171 W by 18.1 on own feel (model pod reserve 24 pct, true maybe 15 pct). Cued ease to 162 ground pace on north leg 3 (about pod 158). Pattern to avoid: surge 170-176 then blow 2 min; steady 158-162 is faster.

text: Cued ease to 162 pace to cap effort near CP after recovery (back at 171 W, would blow again); wake set after turn 3 to retarget for the into-current leg.

arguments.message: Pod reserve reading below 12 pct (true reserve probably near empty): blow-up risk, cap effort

text: no cue: ease-to-162 cue just sent 24 s ago; lowered reserve watch to 12 pct since reading runs high.

arguments.text: Into the current now. Settle to 182 pace, steady rhythm.

Min 20.6 (start leg 4, south): end of leg 3 pod about 160 gave GPS 3.25-3.28 with push_local 0.25-0.30, more than earlier in leg 3 (pod 176 -> 3.21, push_local 0.17); boat-model reserve fell to 0 while pod reserve reads 22 pct. Either current got stronger or pod started reading low (drift). Test on leg 4: at pod about 160, GPS about 2.65-2.7 means stronger current; about 2.85-2.95 means pod reads low. Cued ease to 182 pace (compromise).

arguments.reason: leg 4 test: compare GPS speed at pod power vs leg 2 (leg 2: pod 165, GPS 2.83) to tell current change from pod drift

text: Cued ease to 182 pace for the into-current leg (pod 175 after turn, above CP); wake in 2 min to test current change vs pod drift.

arguments.reason: cue gate opens: drag alert after turn 3 (push_local -0.55 vs fitted -0.18, pod 190 W for GPS 2.57). If still far below fitted push with clean post-turn data, cue clear_rudder (weed?) else ease (pod over CP chasing 182 target).

arguments.text: Min 20.9 drag alert: right after turn 3 push_local fell from +0.18..+0.30 (end of leg 3) to -0.55..-0.60 on leg 4; pod 190 W but GPS 2.57 (leg 2: pod 165 -> 2.83). Two explanations: weed on rudder (picked up at the turn) or wind from the south strengthening (leg 3 push rose 0.17 -> 0.30 before the turn). Test: clear_rudder; if speed recovers it was weed. Paddler 9/10, close to my limit, mentions nothing.

text: no cue: gate closed 45 s; drag alert after turn 3 (weed or wind), will decide clear_rudder vs ease when gate opens.
no cue: gate closed 31 s; pod 219 W chasing 182 target into heavy drag or headwind, blow-up likely; pending wake at gate opening will test clear_rudder, then re-target slower.
